factual_methodology.summary: Validated dated institutional anchors against financial releases: Microsoft FY2026 $329.1bn leases not commenced, recognized $21.925bn operating/$66.594bn finance leases; Oracle FY27 Q1 $664bn RPO versus FCF negative $5bn; Meta 2026 Q2/Q3 capex $31.08/$34.91bn and Q3 FCF negative $2.12bn; CoreWeave Jun $104bn backlog, Nvidia Q2 FY27 $89bn data-center sales. IEA 485TWh 2025, 950TWh 2030 forecast. IMF Oct 14 transaction study $300bn equity, $650bn debt and $1.4tn future revenues are not additive.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Distinct economic thesis linking historic technological cycles to current cash-flow timing, 2026 issuer finance, 19 causal chapters, hardware/depreciation and coding/AI product technical debt, power supply, competition, geopolitics and three discriminating forward scenarios.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two correctly qualified, numerically identical charts in English and Brazilian Portuguese, three analytical Markdown tables, one causal-flow diagram and one qualitative geographic exposure map; no source-inconsistent numeric overlays.

research_depth.summary: Over 6,500 words per locale, 20 substantive level-two headings each, 32 matched research citations across 22 hosts and causal mechanisms with counterfactual tests.

evidence_traceability.summary: Primary annual and quarterly company statements, central banks/IMF/BIS/IEA, 2026 Stanford AI Index, NBER research, NIST/FTC and DORA; explicitly qualify UBP forecasts, Google/GitClear code-quality surveys and hypothetical model economics.

counterfactual_review.summary: Acknowledges real cloud and chip revenues, strong adoption and some productivity gains as contrary evidence to pure speculative fiction; avoids universalizing METR task-level slowdown; differentiates resilient hyperscalers, specialized providers and credit market tail scenarios.

contrary_evidence: AI suppliers and cloud divisions report large realized revenue and deployment, inconsistent with zero commercial adoption.
NBER/Stanford find significant AI adoption; DORA finds positive results in disciplined organizations, contrary to universal technical harm.
METR 2025 task-level slowdown does not estimate economy-wide developer productivity in 2026.
Central banks identify financing fragility, but do not establish a systemic default wave today.
limitations: Financial data mix current filings, earlier vintages and analyst projections with explicit descriptions; no sum of incompatible stocks and flows.
Private AI firms and nonbank deals have limited disclosure; contingent obligations and counterparty chains remain incompletely measured.
Engineering and productivity studies may have selection and observability biases; no aggregate causal estimate is asserted.
IEA 2030 projection is a scenario, not measured future electricity demand.
Numbers are not an independently consolidated financial-system ledger; circular contracts can appear in multiple counterparties.
Illustrative hardware depreciation is not an actual issuer chip price or a forecast.
DORA, METR, GitClear and enterprise surveys have different populations, research designs and causal strengths.
notes: Manual and source-level bilingual QA of exact stage Git blobs, subject to independent CI build and separate production HTTP confirmation. Prose-only correction of prohibited report self-reference, staged and public Markdown matched byte-for-byte; no claim, numbers or sources changed.
